Natural and Synthetic Fragrance Materials Sectional Committee, PCD 18

FOREWORD This Indian Standard (Third Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the drafl finalized by the Natural and Synthetic Fragrance Materials Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. This standard was first published in 1961 and revised in 1975 and 1993. This revision was necessitated by improved production techniques, raw material sources and opening up of the global markets. This standard is in line with the corresponding International Standard. Requirement for pseudo ionone content has been retained in this revision, as a content exceeding two percent is known to develop photosensitization. Ionone (CIJHZOO)(Molecular weight 192.30), as commercially available, is mainly a mixture of two isomers, namely, alpha- and beta-ionone. The alpha-, beta- and gamma-isomers of the material have the following structural formula: Alpha-Ionone Beta-Ionone Gamma-Ionone

4-(2,6,6-Trimethyl-2cyclohexenyl) 3buten-2-one

4-(2,6,6-Trimethyl-l cyclohexenyl) 3buten-2-one

4-(2-Methylene, 6, 6dimethyl, cyclohexyl) 3buten-2-one

Ionones are widely used as basic constituents of violet type perfumes and as modifiers in other floral compositions. The composition of ionones varies widely in the proportion of alpha- and beta- isomers. The source of ionone at present is organic synthesis starting from citral and condensing with acetone to form pseudo ionone, which is then cyclized by acid type reagents. This revision has become-necessary because citral used presently is mostly from synthetic route from turpentine and/or petrochemical route, while previous method used citral isolated horn Iemongrass oil. lonone available in the trade is mostly mixed ionones. For specific applications, the isomers such as alpha and beta are separated. The type of acid used determines the type of isomer formed. T-hisstandard covers all the three grades of ionones commercially available. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value observed or calculated expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revise@)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for ionone. 2 REFERENCES The following standards contain provisions, which, through reference in this text, constitute provisions of this standard. The material shall be a synthetic product, clear liquid, free from sediment, suspended matter and adulterants, when examined as prescribed in IS 326 (Part 2). 5.2 Volubility The material of all grades shall be soluble in three volumes of ethanol (70 percent by volume) when tested as prescribed in IS 326 (Part 6). 5.3 The material shall also comply with the requirements given in Table 1. 6 PACKING
6.1 Packing AND MARKING

(Part 3) :1980 (Part 5) :1986 (Part 6) :1986 (Part 19) :1998 1070:1992 2284:1988

The material shall be supplied in airtight and preferably amber-coloured glass, aluminium, tin-plate containers or any other suitable containers, permitting a minimum of air space, as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. 6.1.1 The material shall be protected from light and stored in a cool and dry place. 6.2 Marking Each container so packed shall bear legibly the following information: a) Name of the material; b) Name of the manufacturer; c) Batch number and date of manufacturer; d) Net and gross weight; and e) Flash point. 6.2.1 BIS Cert@ation Marking The containers may also be marked with the Standard Mark. 6.2.1.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The details of conditions under which the Iicence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards. 1

3 TERMINOLOGY For the purpose of this standard, definitions given in IS 6597 shall apply. 4 GRADES There shall be three grades of the material, namely: .a) Alpha-ionone; b) Beta-ionone; and c) Ionone-pure.

Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS.
Review of Indian Standards

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards shou Id ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Catalogue' and `Standards: Monthly Additions'.
